newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Kubo says he and PM cautious on extra budget.
newsitem.headline: Japan Kubo says he and PM cautious on extra budget.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday that both he and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto were cautious about drafting a supplementary budget featuring a large amount of public works spending.

Kubo also said he and Hashimoto held the view that a supplementary budget should be submitted at the beginning of the regular parliament session starting in January and be adopted as soon as possible.
A supplementary budget with big public spending ought to be formed within this year if it is to be effective, he said.

"The debate and decision (on the extra budget) ought to be around next February," Kubo said, adding that the supplementary budget should centred on covering necessary costs, such as reconstruction after the Kobe earthquake of 1995.
Kubo also urged the government to review overall spending as the country was burdened with large government debt.

Regarding a World Trade Organisation (WTO) ruling that Japan's liquor taxes treat foreign products unfairly, Kubo said: "I'm sure liquor taxes would be reviewed with the WTO ruling in mind during the tax reform discussions for next fiscal year (starting April)."
Details on what kind of reforms would be made had yet to be decided, he added.
Commenting on Bill Clinton's re-election as U.S. president, Kubo said it had been expected and that there was no need to reconsider Japan's policy toward the United States.
"We will pay attention to what the U.S. has to say, but we will continue to make our own decisions on fiscal matters," Kubo said.
Kubo said that with the U.S. presidential election over, he hoped for a prompt start and progress in bilateral insurance talks with the United States.
The agreed deadline to resolve the ongoing dispute to liberalise Japan's insurance market is December 15.
